title: A fan letter about Larry's tone; bird imitations
summary: Harry recalls a radio listener's letter praising Larry's tone, and clarinetists imitating animals, but says he never did that.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: I had a letter at home that Larry got when he was in New York. He was with the Dixieland Band. He got a letter from someone, I think, in Minnesota. That was in the early years of radio. And they did a broadcast of radio. This fellow picks up the program and he listened. He was very attentive. Evidently a clarinet player. And he wrote Larry a letter about his tone. And he expressed himself in saying that... Larry's breathing... He said the way he would breathe, you know. He evidently even heard that. Well, myself, I wouldn't pay much attention to that. He said... And his clarinet must have been superb. You know, his... Well, everything was superb. There wasn't a click or nothing. His tone was so wonderful. And he asked Larry to write him. And he explained his tone. How he got the tone. How he would blow. What type of mouthpiece. And the reed he used. What kind of a clarinet. And all that, you know. I had the letter up until a couple of years ago. If it's still at home, I don't know. But I thought it was wonderful.
Yeah. Nice to have him. Appreciate it. That was in the early years of radio.
The early 20s. 1920s. The early 20s, yeah. And Larry kept that letter for years. I was just thinking about...

I was just thinking about... In the livery stable blues at the rooster call or whatever. Reminds me of Raymond Burke always said he doesn't like livery stable. He can't do that. He can't make livery stables. Do you know... Do you remember when you were a kid or anything when Larry first developed those things? Did he practice it at home or... Well, I don't remember... Do it on the job or under or anything?

I don't remember him practicing livery stable blues. Any tune in particular. But I remember when I was a kid, the clarinet players used to imitate birds, you know. Yeah. Different animals on the clarinet. You know. And I thought that... Well, I never did that myself.
Like you did on violin, you remember? Yeah.
Vaudible. Of course it was good. I thought it was real fine. I liked it, but I never did it myself. That's good.
